title: The Quiet Parish
premise: Estate lawyer Hazel Montrose is summoned to the remote village of Ashen Vale to execute a will for a woman who, according to every record, died thirty years ago. The will arrives with two letters: one confessing to a decades-old death ruled accidental, and one promising that 'the rest' will follow if Hazel fails to find who the confessing twin really was. As Hazel digs into the village's tangled alibis—woven by three families to protect one another—they discover the dead woman had an identical twin who vanished the night of the death, and that Hazel's own late mother appears in the parish records. The trial of the surviving confessor forces Hazel to choose between legal truth and human justice; in the end, Hazel proves the confession false, exposes the real killer as the village's beloved vicar, and claims the inheritance—and the found family—the will quietly left to them.
about_author: Ulyana Lockridge is the pen name of a former rural solicitor's clerk who spent years watching small communities keep their secrets behind polite smiles. They write mysteries about people whose identities were decided by others, and about the slow, stubborn work of taking those identities back.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Hazel Montrose, meticulous and emotionally walled-off, receives probate papers for Edith Fairweather—a woman whose death certificate predates the will by thirty years. POV: Hazel. The beat is cold curiosity sharpening into unease as Hazel realizes the documents are flawless, which means someone powerful made them so.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: A second envelope arrives: a handwritten confession to the 1994 drowning of Thomas Fairweather, signed by his wife, followed days later by an unsigned note promising 'more, if you fail.' POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: professional pride curdling into obsession—Hazel never takes a case they can't close.

chapters.title: Ashen Vale
chapters.summary: Hazel travels to the rain-soaked village and meets the vicar, Daniel Croft, whose warmth feels rehearsed. The parish register shows Edith's burial—but no body was ever exhumed. POV: Hazel. Beat: first taste of the village's practiced silence, delivered with tea and kindness.

chapters.title: The Confessor
chapters.summary: In a care home, Hazel meets Marion Fairweather, elderly and lucid, who repeats her confession word for word—too perfectly, like testimony rehearsed by a lawyer. POV: Hazel. Beat: doubt takes root; a confession this clean is a performance, and performances have directors.

chapters.title: Alibi of Three Families
chapters.summary: Hazel maps the night of Thomas's death: the Fairweathers, the Hollis family at the mill, and the Crofts all vouch for each other in identical phrasing. POV: alternating Hazel and a 1994 flashback from teenage Edith. Beat: the alibis aren't memories; they're architecture.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Ground-penetrating radar hired discreetly reveals a second grave beside Edith's—empty, or holding something small. POV: Hazel. Beat: dread deepens into resolve; someone prepared for questions thirty years before Hazel asked them.

chapters.title: What the Mill Knew
chapters.summary: Ruth Hollis, dying and unafraid now, tells Hazel that Edith had an identical twin sister, Iris, who disappeared the same week Thomas drowned. POV: Ruth (framed within Hazel's interview). Beat: grief and fury—the village didn't lose Iris; it erased her.

chapters.title: Letters in My Mother's Hand
chapters.summary: Among Edith's effects, Hazel finds correspondence signed with their mother's maiden name—letters dated after their mother supposedly left the county. POV: Hazel. Beat: identity cracks open; the case has been circling Hazel's own bloodline all along.

chapters.title: The Vicar's Sermon
chapters.summary: Daniel Croft preaches on forgiveness while watching Hazel in the pews. Afterwards he warns, gently, that some truths cost more than they pay. POV: Hazel. Beat: menace wrapped in grace; Hazel understands the unsigned letter came from inside the church.

chapters.title: Marion Recants
chapters.summary: Marion withdraws her confession, claiming Hazel coerced her; her solicitor is the same firm that drafted the impossible will. POV: Marion, then Hazel. Beat: betrayal and vertigo—Hazel realizes they've been cast as a player, not an observer.

chapters.title: Iris
chapters.summary: A photograph surfaces: two identical girls, one smiling, one not. Records show Iris Fairweather emigrated—or did she? A pension was claimed in her name until 2019. POV: Hazel. Beat: hope with teeth; if Iris lived, someone collected her life like wages.

chapters.title: The Empty House
chapters.summary: Hazel breaks into the shuttered Fairweather cottage and finds a child's shoe, a lawyer's ledger, and a wall of clippings—including one about Hazel's mother's disappearance. POV: Hazel. Beat: terror transmuted into purpose; the cottage was a message left waiting.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibi
chapters.summary: Reconstructing the ledger, Hazel finds payments made annually to 'E.M.'—Edith or Marion?—by the parish trust that Daniel Croft now controls. POV: Hazel. Beat: cold clarity; the money kept the silence alive, and the church held the purse.

chapters.title: The Trial Begins
chapters.summary: Marion is charged with Thomas's murder based on her recanted confession; the village closes ranks around her, and around itself. POV: Hazel, testifying. Beat: guilt and defiance—Hazel's investigation may hang an innocent woman for a sin committed against her.

chapters.title: Cross-Examination
chapters.summary: On the stand, Hazel dismantles the timeline using the mill's flood records: the river path was impassable the night Thomas died—he never reached the water. POV: Hazel. Beat: triumph shadowed by fear; the truth now protects Marion but points at someone still living.

chapters.title: The Letter Promised More
chapters.summary: The final unsigned letter arrives mid-trial: a page of Edith's diary naming her killer, torn just above the signature. Someone wants Hazel to finish it. POV: Hazel. Beat: the trap inverts—Hazel stops being hunted and starts hunting.

chapters.title: Vespers
chapters.summary: Hazel confronts Daniel Croft in the empty church with the diary page and the trust ledgers. He admits nothing, but his hands shake over the collection plate. POV: alternating Hazel and Croft. Beat: the predator's mask slips; justice outside the law begins here.

chapters.title: The Night of the Flood
chapters.summary: Full flashback, 1994: Edith witnessed Croft kill Thomas over the trust money; the twins swapped identities to hide Edith, and Marion confessed to buy time. Iris took Edith's name and fled—with Hazel's mother as her ally. POV: Edith/Iris. Beat: devastating compassion; the lie was love.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Marion is acquitted when Hazel produces the flood evidence and the diary fragment; the courtroom turns toward the gallery where Croft sits. POV: Hazel. Beat: catharsis without comfort—the law frees one woman but cannot touch another's killer.

chapters.title: Confession at the Font
chapters.summary: Croft, exposed and abandoned, confesses privately to Hazel—not for forgiveness, but because Edith's will promised publication unless he spoke. He is arrested on fresh evidence Hazel unearthed. POV: Croft, then Hazel. Beat: grim satisfaction; justice arrived late, wearing a lawyer's coat.

chapters.title: The Rest of the Will
chapters.summary: The will's true bequest unfolds: everything goes to 'the child of M., my debt unpaid'—Hazel. Edith knew who Hazel was all along. POV: Hazel. Beat: grief and belonging colliding; invisibility was never chosen for Hazel—it was inherited.

chapters.title: The Quiet Parish
chapters.summary: Spring comes to Ashen Vale. Hazel stays, reopening the cottage, visiting Marion weekly, learning the names on every grave—including Iris's real one, finally marked. POV: Hazel. Beat: quiet resolution; found family isn't discovered, it's built, one honest stone at a time.
